review_text_raw: I love the other Simulacra games, but I waited a while to play this one because it has mixed reviews. I can understand why now and am disappointed...The game feels rushed. It has typos and the dialogue is poor. Gameplay in terms of finding info and doing puzzles is lame/tedious, and there aren't many puzzles at all. Story and characters are underdeveloped. I was also really disappointed to find your choices don't matter that much throughout the game. There are only a few choices that make any difference in dialogue/outcome, which sucks for a game where 90% of the gameplay is choosing dialogue options. I replayed to get all endings and achievements, but we're talking minor changes between outcomes that make replaying the game basically pointless. Overall, not much actually happens to make the game worth your time. Just skip it if you're a fan of the previous games.

review_text_raw:
Loved the first two games and was very excited to start the third. The prospect of a new setting---getting away from depraved online influencers and into a rural area---seemed neat. And we might even be working against a new threat, be it a new mutation of the Simulacra or perhaps a different monster altogether. 

In the previous two games, you get engaged right away.
 
Game 1 starts with the phone glitching out, emitting eerie sounds the second you touch it. Then, as though haunted, it forcibly opens one video among a dozen corrupted files, showing a brief yet shocking video that teases the main mystery: what happened to Anna and is this phone haunted? The video is fragmented and ambiguous but the victim’s distress is very clear. Her final words? “Don’t come looking for me.” Its immediately intriguing. 

In the second game you're a junior detective at the local precinct. It starts with a meeting between you and the chief, where he confides to you the existence of a secret division within the police department, one which handles unnatural phenomena. He hands you stolen evidence: a phone, from the recently deceased Maya, who's strange death frightened the PD regulars into closing her case prematurely. In light of their unwillingness to discover the truth, the chief tasks you personally with spelunking through the phone to unearth clues. He needs your help because he's an older fellow who's not technologically inclined, while you're the young whippersnapper who's hip with the youths and does the iphones. 

Right away there's a sense of urgency. The department is looking for the stolen evidence, you’re breaking the rules just by having this conversation with the chief, and this secret division desperately needs to furnish some results or risk being shut down by the higher ups. And it’s all up to you.

Like the first installment, there’s some spooky phone glitches which show us something is terribly wrong but doesn’t show us exactly what, baiting the mystery.

To help you along, the chief sets you up with cutting edge, AI based software to help you log clues, disseminate evidence, remote hack the victim’s laptop and restore corrupted files. It was developed to help law enforcement conduct investigations which, in our modern world, are increasingly linked to social technology and personal communications. So it’s at least believable. And it imparts a cool-factor, being given access to exclusive, law enforcement tech.

In game three, you’re just some indistinguishable f*ck from the neighborhood watch group. You’re met with a normal phone and some flat, uninteresting dialogue from Ruby, who decides that the best gambit to enlist your assistance is to belittle you, calling you out as the office coffee b*tch and saying “you might know me, I’m the one who’s always ordering the double tall macchiato” or whatever. As if to imply that you, you loathsome, lowly creature, are so far beneath her station that you could only recognize her by the coffees she sends you to fetch like the obedient mud worm you are.

Then, after nailing down just how useless you are, she inexplicably puts her entire case in your hands. And by “inexplicably,” I mean there’s no reason whatsoever for her to need you or trust you at all. She just heedlessly unloads her project—a project that could very easily get her fired—onto you, who she has just thoroughly disrespected.

You get another scanning tool but unlike the WARDEN app from Simulacra 2, this one feels… shoehorned. It was made by some b*tchless basement dweller named Paul, who looks and acts like a sock puppet, who’s tied his unusual app to the GPS. For reasons.

Like its predecessors, you still get to see a creepy video but its overly long and boring. And entirely too blatant. You get to see the cheesy shadow monster, what’s called “the Beldam” (a dumber name I could not fathom) without any preamble or creativity or teasing. Not only that but you stumble across it like it’s just another YouTube video in the shuffle queue. No spooky glitch, no nameless entity forcing you to look at it. Just.. “oh hey neat.”

Somehow, despite the obviousness of the monster video, when you send it to Ruby she instantly decides to go for a stroll in the very same haunted hallway, alone. Which was so unbelievably obtuse it completely shattered any immersion I’d forced myself to conjure just to make it this far.

To make matters even less interesting, everyone in town already seems to know about the Beldam. It’s on their social media, it’s in their photo reels, one @$$hole even talks about seeing its shape in his latte foam. Seriously, wtf? So there’s nothing special about you discovering its existence. Instead of engaging your morbid curiosity and imagination, it just makes you feel like you’re reading hokey bullcrap about bigfoot in a lowbrow tabloid. 

The real nail in this games’ coffin is: instead of giving us one victim to focus on, who’s distress we can directly witness and care about, we’re hit with a list of missing randos who’s peril is entirely unknown to us. They’re just “missing” y’know… kind of like the plot. 

The only threat it draws our attention to, is that a comically greedy mayor wants to pave over the local farmers market and build a mall. 
Wow. 
Call in the national guard. 
Nothing gets me quaking in my boots like the threat of a shopping mall. 

And even then, it’s just plain text. No video, no room for interpretation or imagination. They just black-and-white spell it out for you. “MaYOr bAd, mAke fARmErs sAD.”

This game completely lacks any of the inspiration and vision that made the prequels special. Feels like a cheap cash grab.

Uninstalled.

Overall, I’d recommend skipping this one. While the story itself isn’t bad, the execution is lacking in almost every way.

A step-down from the last two installments. Compared to Simulacra 1 and 2, this is... pretty bad. Meh-ish. Semi-spoilers down below!
I don't mind the game's antagonist. If you've read other reviews where it says it's a ghost, the answer to that is a yes and a no. It's still a simulacra, but it takes a form of a ghost that's popular in the town's folklore and media.
That aside, the devs had made this installment rather boring and plain. You'd expect something more complex and interesting compared to the last game, but it's just... a huge down-grade from that. And I didn't even hate the second one! It was good!
BUUUT! Credit where credit's due: certain sequences are rather tense (like the entirety of Paul's house thing), and it works really well. I quite like the Atlas tracking functions, too. Ruby's actress is good, and Paul's actor is good at voice acting, so it isn't ENTIRELY bad.
Still, if you, like me, wanted to just play every installments of this franchise, just wait for the discount and get the bundle edition, since if you have the last two games, it will save you at least 30 cents if you just bought it seperately.
Overall, the experiance feels like the very first game minus the good with itty bitty of the new. Play at your own risk.

review_text_raw:
Simulacra 3 is a game that is genuinely interesting most of the time. Which is about the biggest compliment I can give it. Now the rest isn't all THAT bad, but it's certainly not on par with Sara is Missing or the original Simulacra. It's a found phone game that could've evolve to be so much more, but instead finds itself stuck with more of the same formulaic problems from previous iterations of the game. Here's some spoiler free bullet points on the game. TLDR at the bottom 

The Story. 
The story is easily the best part of the game. It's fairly interesting, if you've played the previous games, you pick up on a lot of what's going on and the game makes some references to them, but it's definitely not necessary to play the previous games. There's enough of a mystery here that it's kinda neat to unravel. 

Horror 
This is easily the weakest part of the game. I can't express how much I hate this asinine "horror" element. Since the last game, I've called it "Powerpoint horror" because there's moments where the phone glitches and it just sits there. You have to click to advance the glitchiness to increase how scary it is or something. I hate to just openly call out something for being bad design, but imagine you're on a roller coaster. The cart ratchets it's way to the top and you're about to go over the edge. Now you have to use a crank on the side of the roller coaster that lowers you down the drop a few steps at a time. Your stomach never drops, you don't get the adrenaline rush, your arm is getting tired from cranking the cart down though. I really wish this series would knock it off. The first game had loud phone call notifications that would make you jump, but sigh in relief, even a creepy unsettling moment here and there, but this one just tries to use super glitchy video effects. Which brings me to my next complaint. 

VFX
The game is at it's best when you're digging around the phone for answers and the dialogue options to guide people around. However, the absolute worst part is when it relies on fmv green screen vfx to tell a story. Look, I know. The budget doesn't really allow for Marvel movie level vfx, but there's a lot of green screen elements, really cheesy animations, and the acting isn't necessarily the best. I think a lot of the scenes could've been done inexpensively practically, but I'm guessing due to production issues, decisions were made to opt in for vfx instead. The "creepy" shadows and overly aggressive "glitchy" effects aren't really adding a lot to the game. 

The sound design is also particularly horrible in one section of the game. When the game is waiting for your response, the ambient sound levels are maxed out, but when you make a selection, the volume drops back down to normal. Not like a HUGE issue, but it's a glaringly obvious one I feel like should've been very easily caught. 

TLDR; 
The game isn't scary at all. It tries too hard and relies on cheesy vfx, cringey fmv (live action) moments, and puzzles that range from incredibly simple to very vague. Overall the story was just interesting enough for me to finish it, but nothing I'm going to talk about a few days from now.

review_text_raw: The weakest of the Simulacra Trilogy by far (even Pipe Dreams felt more comprehensive as a horror experience). It feels like the budget for this game was severely cut. There are many features missing in this game that were present in the previous, the horror elements are few and far between, and obvious bugs still remaining in the game (as of Sept 2026). The audio mixing clearly has issues with some dialogue being so quiet I have to bump up my volume a considerable amount, only later to have my eardrums blasted by one of Paul's vlog videos. The characters have almost no interesting traits and the writing feels flat. Your responses barely seem to matter for most of the game... what happened to being able to lie convincingly to people over texts? Having your character spill the beans about who they are under the slightest bit of pressure takes all the fun out of choosing unique dialogue. Speaking of the dialogue, it is SLOW with no option for increasing text speed- this made getting all achievements an absolute slog. Overall, I expected more from the final entry in this series. I put off playing this game for a long time because the reviews were very mixed, and this sadly confirmed my expectations of the quality of this game. Maybe pick this up if you still want more Simulacra after playing the first two games, but don't expect the same level of quality.

review_text_raw:
After enjoying the first two games I thought I was highly anticipating the release for the 3rd one. Sadly this one falls to deliver  anything close to resembling as a interesting/fun game. Even for  9 dollars, at full price. I feel like I wasted money (not rings of power money though). The phone is completely worthless other than what your supposed to do with it at the time, so it doesn't really feel like discovering a person's phone just kinda getting hand held throughout the game. Seems like they went with less "aps" this time, because you use the same ap (atlas) to get from a map feed to a twitter feed. When I called 911 this time around just nothing happens, instead of some somewhat funny dialogue or something else. 411, or dialing 0 also nothing. Trying to call a few people just has calls getting dropped as well which was always kinda a whatever thing, but it's the little things that keep you kinda engaged in story your telling here.

The two characters in the game are very one dimensional. You even though you have the protagonist's  phone you really don't learn anything of interest about this character outside of his drive to stop the plot of the story.  I didn't feel like I was sneaking a peak into his life with loaded with embarrassing messages from maybe his mom,  cringey selfies he taken, or some random thing he bought or really anything that makes the Protagonist feel like a real character. It felt like all information given was utilized to further the plot which made the game feel much more hollow.  

The only other character that you interact with is also just as bland as the main sadly, despite I think the actress trying very hard to work with very bad writing. (I get the lack of pronouns here, but getting called "ROOK" after I just saved your life like a bunch of times was laughable.) Sadly you don't care about saving any of these people, or this town which really feels like the bulk of work was put into. Basically this town is the main character here... Well it's like trying to save Westeros  without meeting anyone who lived there. No one really gives a crap about it. It's actually such a downgrade from either of the previous two games in this retrospect I'm surprised the same company made this game. 

 Nothing was particularly creepy about this one either, Couple times some creepy things happened while I was searching on the phone but it was very minor. The videos that were supposed to be creepy just looked kinda silly, but I understand it's 9 dollars....and  I'm sure there's quite a bit I missed in my first play though, but honestly I have no desire to go back through and get the other "endings" which endings have typically been very weak for the series anyways... I mean could we actually go somewhere with this? I feel like the developers are just trying to milk what was at first a very engaging dynamic and just throwing it into any pot the can stir here. Can like we be maybe a member of an X-FIles unit and maybe we're getting to the bottom of how all Simulcras originated from? or a literal ton of other directions we can actually take??  Sorry on game 3 just having that your phone/ap can kill people is a played out concept. I feel bad writing this, but this game feels so half-assed and disappointing to me who was a big fan of the series I felt betrayed by what should've been a solid stamp on a decent trilogy here.
